notes: An RNG roller with rarities, a luck stat, a pity counter, a currency shop and a rarest-roll leaderboard is the incremental family, which is Simulation — the number going up is the game, and the 3D world is the lobby it happens in. The scale answer pins one compact floating island crossed in a few seconds, so I took space-bounded from the catalogue rather than the genre's typical world-open, whose Shared Persistent World wording assumes a world explored over distance; the smaller background islands are backdrop that nobody crosses, so island-cluster would have added a CHECK for scenery and I left it as skybox dressing. Incremental Simulator is the preset, with the ROLL platform landing on station-training as the repeatable pad that raises the number, the inventory and shop buildings on social-hub, and gate-progression dropped because nothing here is walled off behind a purchase — rarity is random rather than ground you unlock. Decided without a user: no SET, since players still walk the island between spawn, the roll pad and the shop fronts, and no building-interior, because the author says the shop and inventory are used from outside — which keeps this entirely on P0.
